name: Coppery-headed Emerald
rangeDescription: Highlands of northern and central costa rica
description: Small hummingbird with obviously decurved bill. Male mostly glittering green with coppery crown and bright white outer tail feathers; female similar but with white underparts.

name: Palani Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Southern india (palni and anaimalai hills and northern kerala)
description: This is the only montane laughingthrush in its range and hence unmistakable. It has dull olive-brown upperparts, a grey-streaked white breast, and a rufous-chestnut lower breast and belly.

name: Hermit Wood-Wren
rangeDescription: Temperate and upper subtropical santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Small, short-tailed wren endemic to the Santa Marta Mountains of Colombia. It has a white eyebrow and streaky face, though plumage is almost identical to that of Gray-breasted Wood-Wren.

name: Cirl Bunting
rangeDescription: Northwestern africa (morocco eastward to northwestern tunisia); southwestern england (formerly also wales); southern europe from the iberian peninsula and france eastward to romania and western and northern türkiye, also the balearics, corsica, sardinia, sicily, and crete; introduced new zealand
description: Male distinctive, with striking head and breast pattern, especially blackish throat. Female drab and streaky, told from Yellowhammer by finer dark streaking, more boldly striped head, and grayish rump (not bright rusty).

name: Long-billed Wren-Babbler
rangeDescription: Eastern himalayas (sikkim to eastern assam and northeastern myanmar)
description: Streaky, short-tailed brown bird with a long, slightly decurved bill; the only wren-babbler in its range to have a long bill. Long pale streaks all over the body give it a slick-feathered appearance.

name: Black Solitaire
rangeDescription: West slope of western andes of colombia (chocó) and northwestern ecuador
description: This striking thrush is unmistakable if seen well: mostly jet black with a white cheek, white tuft under the shoulder, and white outer tail feathers (easily visible from below). Also note red eye and orange lower mandible.

name: Red-bellied Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Eastern north america (southern canada to texas and florida keys)
description: Medium-sized woodpecker that is not well named; rarely is the slight red wash on the belly visible! Instead, note the black-and-white barring on the back and wings, plain buffy breast and face, and red nape.

name: Pale-bellied Tyrant-Manakin
rangeDescription: Lower amazonian brazil; central and eastern brazil to northeastern bolivia
description: A nondescript manakin that is reminiscent of a flycatcher. It is olive-green above and gray below with faint streaks on the breast.

name: Rufous-breasted Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to eastern ecuador, western venezuela, and northern peru
description: Fairly distinctive small flycatcher found in the Andes from western Venezuela to northwest Peru. Rather lanky and long-tailed with obvious rufous wash on face and breast and two rufous wingbars.

name: Cinnamon-faced Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Andean foothills of central and southeastern peru and adjacent northern bolivia
description: Small yellowish tyrannulet with a narrow reddish facial patch. Usually perches horizontally in the mid-story and canopy of humid montane forest.

name: Socotra Cisticola
rangeDescription: Socotra (off eastern somalia)
description: Small, pale brown, heavily streaked cisticola. Endemic to Socotra, where it inhabits low shrublands and other habitats with significant bushy cover, mostly at low elevations.

name: Rameron Pigeon
rangeDescription: Ethiopia to eastern democratic republic of the congo, tanzania, and south africa; western angola
description: Big, dark pigeon with a gray head, and bright yellow feet, bill, and eye ring. Plain in flight.

name: Perija Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Sierra de perijá, colombia (and venezuela?)
description: The only tapaculo found in the Perijá Mountains, which straddle the Colombia-Venezuela border north of the main chain of the Andes. Adult is gray with brown rump and lower underparts.

name: Giant Weaver
rangeDescription: São tomé (gulf of guinea)
description: A spectacular enormous weaver endemic to São Tomé, with a robust barbet-like bill and a bulky head. Adult male has a black head and a chestnut collar that extends to the breast.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Violet-tailed Sunbird
rangeDescription: Cameroon to gabon, northeastern angola, central african republic, and northeastern democratic republic of the congo
description: An iridescent sunbird of forest and forest edge, almost always near water. Males are distinctly bicolored: iridescent purple on their tails and heads and white on their bellies, with iridescent green highlights on the wings and orange underwing tufts.

name: Congo Moor Chat
rangeDescription: Gabon to southern angola, central african republic, and western democratic republic of the congo
description: An unusual and distinctive Central African chat. Mostly gray-brown with a white throat, rump, and undertail and white wing patches that are conspicuous in flight.

name: Mountain Owlet-nightjar
rangeDescription: Mountains of new guinea, from the bird's head peninsula, the wandammen mountains, and the foja mountains, through central new guinea to the huon and southeastern peninsulas
description: A small owlet-nightjar of montane forests. Dark head, pale collar, barred back and tail.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Bahia Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Montane forest of southeastern brazil (southern bahia near boa nova)
description: Small flycatcher with a long tail that is usually held cocked. Has an olive-green back, a whitish throat, and yellowish underparts.

name: Oriole Cuckooshrike
rangeDescription: Southern cameroon to southwestern central african republic, eastern democratic republic of the congo, and gabon
description: A spectacular cuckooshrike that resembles an oriole, with a yellow-green back, wings and tail, yellow underparts, a dark head and bill, and large fleshy orange wattles under the eyes. The sexes differ slightly: the head of the male is jet black and the female has a less contrasting brownish head.

name: Luzon Rail
rangeDescription: Montane north-central luzon (northern philippines); few recent records
description: A mysterious medium-sized rail, possibly of foothill or montane grassy areas and forests. Dark brown above with a pale gray chest, a whitish throat, a barred belly, blackish legs, and a fairly long, curved reddish bill.
